claims.text: Dynamic rafting of precipitates enhances the creep resistance of dual-phase FCC/BCC high-entropy-alloy protective coatings during continuous high-temperature loading.
The starting coating consists primarily of an FCC matrix containing dispersed BCC precipitates.
The starting precipitates are randomly dispersed and unrafted in the as-deposited or as-cast state.
There is an inherent positive lattice misfit between the FCC matrix and the BCC precipitates.
Positive lattice misfit drives stress-assisted dislocation climb during continuous loading.
Stress-assisted dislocation climb facilitates precipitate coarsening.
Stress-assisted dislocation climb facilitates alignment and rafting of the precipitates.
Positive misfit can produce a parallel raft microstructure during creep.
Aligned BCC precipitates act as pinning barriers to dislocation motion.
Dislocation pinning by the rafted precipitates reduces the creep strain rate.
High-temperature loading will produce aligned BCC precipitate rafts relative to the initial unrafted microstructure.
The high-temperature-loaded sample will develop a refined precipitate structure.
Raft development will correlate with a lower creep strain rate than the starting baseline under identical loading conditions.
Raft development will delay the onset of tertiary creep.
The proposed mechanism is active above approximately 600 °C, where diffusion-driven processes are active.
At lower temperatures, rafting may not develop noticeably.
Rafting may not develop when stress is insufficient to activate significant dislocation climb.
Low-temperature annealing will inhibit rafting and preserve a suitable baseline control state.

contradictions.description: The mechanism predicts precipitate coarsening during rafting, whereas the predicted outcome calls the resulting structure refined; these descriptions imply opposing size evolution unless refinement is separately defined.

The predicted outcome requires comparison under identical loading conditions, but the proposed groups are maintained under low-temperature annealing versus sustained high-temperature loading. This changes temperature and loading history along with rafting and therefore does not provide the stated identical-condition comparison.
